review: focused read-only review of frozen resume jobs implementation

reviewed_boundaries.grant_parser: The flat JSON parser accepts only one nxm property and bounded ASCII content; URI parsing requires the exact nxm scheme/game/mods/id/files/id shape, canonical positive signed-63 values and exactly one literal key/expires/user_id query field. Percent decoding is bounded and rejects malformed escapes, nonprintable bytes and raw plus-space conversion. Fragments, ports, userinfo, extra paths/query fields and scope mismatch fail closed.
reviewed_boundaries.resume_admission: The ABI validates structure, span overlap, cookie/CSRF/Origin and lowercase job ID; it performs fresh account admission, searches only same-cookie ownership, and only accepts a needs_nexus_authorization record with no pending grant. Parsed scope must match retained game/mod/file. The same ID, source, kind, idempotency key and slot are retained; full source capacity does not block resume.
reviewed_boundaries.commit_and_cleanup: Parsed and staged grants are wiped through RAII. Output is serialized before fresh account/session, storage/directory, expiry and monotonic-time gates; failures clear output length and output RAII wipes its full capacity. The final record assignment is non-failing and follows all gates. Free, bindings_clear and fail_record erase stored grants.
reviewed_boundaries.worker_consume: run_one copies then clears the queued grant before resolution, builds a distinct typed grant whose domain does not alias the source domain, and wipes both local grant structures immediately after resolver return and before archive transfer. Authorization-required is preserved for the late-link expiry case; account and other resolver failures are not broadly remapped.

evidence_scope: Static review only. No tests, builds, provider calls, credentials, console operations or source edits were made. The owner reported focused component controls for initial and late-link expiry/fresh retry; this review does not independently claim that execution evidence.
